purpose: Determine whether finite populations persist long enough for long-horizon trait stationarity to be biologically interpretable, after the deterministic-density extension entered sub-individual mass regimes.
primary_endpoints: paired near-and-far occupancy at each checkpoint
extinction-time distribution by arm and depression
far-minus-near investment effect among paired survivors, explicitly survivor-conditioned

interpretation_gate.otherwise: long-horizon trait endpoints are survivor-conditioned and cannot be described as a population-wide stationary evolutionary regime

claim_boundary: Finite-population persistence is the primary long-horizon endpoint; survivor-conditioned traits cannot substitute for extinction.
6400 reproductive seasons are not 6400 calendar years for perennials and are not geological time.
This diagnostic was designed after observing the deterministic-density sub-individual-mass problem; it is a new prospective diagnostic, not part of the original preregistration.
No horizon, depression level, history, start, or demographic seed is added or removed after finite outcomes are inspected.
The stationary visitor process is a stress scenario rather than a reconstruction of natural island history.
retirement_reason: The depression-0.75 deterministic long-horizon route was already non-interpretable at the focal season because it crossed the persistence boundary, while the focal depression-0.50 repeatability claim was resolved by occupied finite-population analyses and two prospective repeatability validations. Running 12,288 trajectories to 6,400 seasons would not adjudicate the current manuscript headline and would add a stationary-environment stress test outside the submission claim.
retirement_boundary: Retirement is a scope decision, not a successful or failed simulation result.
The frozen unexecuted design is retained for provenance and could be revived only as a separate future stress-test question.
No manuscript claim is based on unexecuted finite-long-horizon outcomes.
